title: perf-bench-scratch-olivia-khan-2026-03-06
content:
Personal scratchpad - perf experiments 2026-03-06

Objective: quick latency/throughput comparison for Llama2-13B variants under different batching and kv-cache configs. Goal to pick default serving profile for hosted-api and dedicated pools.

Hardware
- A100 40GB (single GPU per worker)
- Triton + custom runtime build (opt-level: kernel-selection v2)

Models / Builds
- llama2-13b (fp16 baseline)
- llama2-13b-q4 (4-bit quant, Q4_K_ML variant)
- llama2-13b-q4-kvcache (same quant, KV cache enabled in runtime)

Test harness
- Synthetic prompt set: 500 unique prompts sampled from prod prompt-corpus (avg tokens: 38, sd: 12)
- Sequence length used: 256 (prompt) + generation up to 128 tokens
- Batching: [1,4,8,16] request-level batch sizes
- Concurrency: 8 clients / worker
- Metrics: p50, p95, p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (overall), GPU memory usage
- Measurement method: 5 warmup runs, aggregate metrics over 3x 10k request runs

Key results (summary)
- Baseline fp16, batch=1: p50=95ms, p95=210ms, tokens/sec=18k
- q4 batch=1: p50=110ms, p95=240ms, tokens/sec=16.5k (slower single-request latency due to dequant/packing overhead)
- q4 + KV cache batch=1 (cache hits ~65%): p50=65ms, p95=130ms, tokens/sec=24k (KV cache massively benefits repeated context)
- fp16 batch=8: p50=260ms, p95=560ms, tokens/sec=98k (good throughput, worse tail latency)
- q4 batch=8: p50=310ms, p95=720ms, tokens/sec=110k (throughput slightly higher vs fp16 but p95 worse)

Observations
- KV cache provides best user-perceived latency for interactive workloads with repeated prefixes - p50 drops ~30-40ms vs fp16.
- Quantization (q4) increases single-request latency due to decode overhead, but improves throughput at higher batch sizes (more compute-bound efficiency).
- Tail latencies (p95/p99) grow sharply with batching; need to balance SLOs for interactive routes.
- Memory usage: q4 reduces GPU memory footprint by ~35%, enabling higher concurrency per GPU or larger batch sizes.
- Triton kernel-selection v2 shows 8-12% improvement over previous build for long sequences; need to validate across more seq lengths.

Quick recommendations
- For latency-sensitive hosted-api chat route: use fp16 + KV cache enabled + request-level batching capped at 4.
- For throughput-oriented embedding/batch-gen workloads: use q4 with batch sizes 8-16 and dedicate pools.
- Add a 'kv-cache warmup' step for canary rollouts to avoid cold-cache tail spikes.

Next steps / TODOs
- Run full sweep across sequence lengths [128,256,512] and measure p95 sensitivity (assign to Samira)
- Validate q4 quantization profile Q4_K_ML vs Q4_HF (file a PR for model build: GH #452 assigned to Ethan)
- Add end-to-end test in perf-suite that simulates mixed workload (30% repeated prompts) to quantify KV cache benefit
- Create a short doc for Console team with recommended defaults per route (draft for product-hosted-api)

Notes to self
- Watch out for measurement noise: ensure same docker image across runs
- Save raw logs: s3://perf-logs/olivia/2026-03-06/ (will upload after cleanup)

Unresolved questions
- How does q4 behave on T4 vs A100 for identical workloads? (need small cluster test)
- Is there an efficient way to prefill KV cache for canary users without leaking context? (privacy + perf tradeoff)

Raw links / refs
- Perf harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness
- PR for triton kernel changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/452

End of scratchpad.
